items.title: An essentially finite type injective local homomorphism out of a geometrically unibranch local domain with separable residue extension is the localization of an etale map
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a geometrically unibranch local domain (A, m) and an injective local homomorphism A -> B of local rings, essentially of finite type, such that mB is the maximal ideal of B and the induced residue field extension is separable, and concludes that A -> B is the localization of an etale ring map (source lines 31817-31828). The proof is a reduction-and-descent argument. It writes B = C_q with A -> C of finite type and q a prime over m, and uses the unramifiedness criterion to see that A -> C is unramified at q (proof lines 31831-31835). The structure proposition for unramified maps then supplies, after replacing C by a principal localization, a standard etale ring map A -> C' with a surjection C' -> C; taking q' the inverse image of q and B' = C'_{q'} gives a surjection B' -> B, and it remains to show it is also injective (proof lines 31836-31842). That is the substantive step: since A is a domain the rings C' and B' are reduced, and since A is geometrically unibranch B' is a domain, using the invariance of the number of branches under smooth maps and the branch-count-one criterion (proof lines 31845-31849). If B' -> B were not injective, then A cap Ker(B' -> B) would be nonzero by the nonzero-contraction lemma, contradicting the injectivity of A -> B (proof lines 31850-31852). The non-routine content is the recognition that geometric unibranchness forces the standard etale cover to be a domain, which is what upgrades surjectivity to an isomorphism.
